verdict.line: You lose if you tank Darius's early Q/AA trades and get chained into an E pull before level 3; you win if you dash-dodge his engage and force isolated all-ins from level 6 on, where the numbers say you have the sniping edge.

brief.thesis: This is a 49.2% win rate over 885 games because both champions are built to win extended 1v1s, but the way they get there differs: Darius wins by stacking Hemorrhage and forcing you into his E (Apprehend) pull radius, while you win by using E (Umbral Dash)'s two charges to dodge that pull and then out-sustain him with passive healing once the fight is already happening. Whoever dictates the terms of the all-in wins it, and OP.GG's own solo-kill data says that's you.

theirWindow.when: E is up and you're near a minion wave edge
theirWindow.what: Darius only threatens a real engage when E (Apprehend) is off cooldown — the outer half of the axe hitbox is what pulls, so staying centered on the wave or behind minions denies the grab entirely. If you see him walk up with E ready, back off half a step rather than trading face-first.

yourWindow.when: his E is down or both your E charges are up
yourWindow.what: This is when the 'solo-kill advantage' actually shows up on the screen. Dash in with E (Umbral Dash) for the heal-on-hit, land Q (Dark Blade) for the knock-up on the outer edge, and chain your empowered auto from passive Deathbringer's Stance — with his pull denied he has no way to reset the trade in his favor.

start.why: The 48.8% win rate sample (860 games, 76.5% pick) confirms this is the standard start — the extra sustain and damage matter because you want to be the one initiating short trades, not surviving his.

boots.why: OP.GG's own tip flags this directly: Steelcaps blunt both his auto-attack poke and his Q (Decisive Strike) hits, which is what lets you actually close distance without shredding your HP bar first. 84% pick rate at 48.9% win confirms it's the default, not a situational pick.

core.why: The burst-and-shield proc rewards exactly the kind of isolated all-in you're looking for post-6, and it's the anchor of the highest-winrate path measured (56.7% over 67 games).
Crit-triggered healing on your first hit stacks with your passive's own lifesteal, which is the mechanical reason your extended fights outlast his bleed damage.
Damage-over-time conversion directly counters his bleed stacks and Q execute-style burst — this is the item that turns 'even' trades into wins late.

situational.when: he's building tanky (Black Cleaver > Sundered Sky path hit 60.6% over 33 games) or their team is stacking armor
the game is going long and you're weaving abilities every fight rather than single-target dueling
you need the dash-reset burst to punish him before he can land a second E
their comp shifts toward AP damage or heavy CC beyond just Darius

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking Conqueror in extended trades is what actually realizes your solo-kill edge — it converts prolonged fights (which favor you) into more damage and healing the longer the duel runs, which is the opposite of what Darius's burst-bleed kit wants.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 88.9% of games at 49% win because Ignite both denies his Q (Decisive Strike) heal on a reset and secures the solo kills this matchup is already tilted toward — Flash is your dodge for a mistimed E pull or his R (Noxian Guillotine) execute range.

playing.title: Hug the wave pre-6
playing.detail: Before you have R, never stand at the outer edge of minions where Darius's E (Apprehend) hook can catch you — the axe only pulls from its far arc, so staying centered denies his entire engage tool.

playing.title: Trade off cooldowns, not face-to-face
playing.detail: Only extend a trade when your Q or E is up to land the knock-up or heal — trading autos into his passive Hemorrhage just feeds his stack count for free.

playing.title: Count his bleed stacks
playing.detail: Five stacks of Hemorrhage means his next ability hits harder and his R execute threshold gets easier to reach — disengage below 40% HP once he's stacked rather than trading through it.

playing.title: Save one E charge to punish
playing.detail: Don't dump both charges of E (Umbral Dash) just to poke — keep one in reserve so you can immediately follow up the instant his E (Apprehend) misses or goes on cooldown.

playing.title: All-in the instant his E is down
playing.detail: This is the literal mechanical reason the solo-kill stat favors you — with his pull denied, dash in, land Q's edge knock-up, and let passive Deathbringer's Stance's empowered auto close the fight.

playing.title: Don't get baited by his R range
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine has real range and resets on kill — never dip below the true-damage execute threshold near his ultimate cooldown, even if you're 'winning' the trade on paper.

playing.title: Play for post-6 sustain fights
playing.detail: Your R (World Ender) rewards fights that drag on; his rewards fights that end fast. Kite half a second, force him to commit Q and E, then re-engage once his cooldowns are down.

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, pick rates, item paths, runes, and summoner splits above are measured OP.GG data from real games on the current patch — the tactical reasoning (why the trades and timings play out that way) is my own read on top of those numbers.

stats.opponentTip: Do not get pulled by Darius’s (E). Purchase Plated Steelcaps first to manage your distance properly. Try to engage him whenever your abilities come off cooldown.
